issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The danger only shows up in a crash, when the driver air bag can burst with too much force.
issues.why: The Takata inflator in the driver air bag uses a propellant that breaks down after years of heat and humidity. In a crash it can rupture and throw metal pieces. Every Element model year is covered, and some replacement inflators from earlier repairs were recalled again.
issues.next: Check your VIN now and have the inflator replaced for free. An Element that never had the repair is at high risk.

issues.t: Passenger air bag inflator can rupture (Takata recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. In a collision the front passenger air bag can burst and spray metal fragments.
issues.why: The passenger-side Takata inflator has the same propellant breakdown. Several recalls cover Elements depending on year and the state where the car was registered.
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free replacement. Until then, avoid carrying a front passenger.

issues.t: Automatic transmission bearing can break and cause stalling or rollaway (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, the transmission makes grinding noises, or the car can roll after being put in Park.
issues.why: A bearing race on the automatic transmission secondary shaft can break from hard downshifts. Honda recalled these Elements for a software update that changes shift control to protect the bearing.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN and make sure the software update was done. Always set the parking brake when parked.

issues.t: Soft or sinking brake pedal from air in the stability control unit (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or sinks farther toward the floor than normal.
issues.why: Air can get into the stability control (VSA) brake modulator over time. Honda recalled these Elements to bleed the air out and seal the unit.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN. If the pedal feels soft, have the brakes checked before driving more.

issues.t: Left rear trailing arm bracket can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the left rear, the car pulling, or poor handling.
issues.why: On 241 cars the bracket for the left rear trailing arm bushing was not welded properly and could come apart. Owners were told to stop driving until it was inspected.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Do not drive an affected car until the arm has been inspected and replaced.

issues.t: Shift cable may be set wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The transmission may not go into the gear you select, the shifter position does not match the gear, or the key will not come out.
issues.why: On some 2010 automatic Elements built April to June 2010, the shift cable was not set correctly. Honda recalled them to reset it.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the cable adjusted.

issues.t: Trailer turn signals only work with the brakes on (recall)
issues.sym: When towing, the trailer turn signals do not flash unless you press the brake pedal.
issues.why: The Honda trailer hitch wiring harness had the turn signal and brake light wires swapped. Honda recalled it.
issues.next: If you tow with a Honda harness, check your VIN and have the wiring corrected.

issues.t: Loud rattle for a few seconds on cold start (VTC actuator)
issues.sym: A grinding or rattling noise for one or two seconds right after starting a cold engine, sometimes with a check engine light for cam timing.
issues.why: The VTC actuator (variable cam timing gear) on the 2.4L engine can let the timing chain rattle before oil pressure builds. A worn chain tensioner can add to it. Honda revised the actuator design.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the actuator checked. If the noise only lasts a second and there are no codes, it is not urgent, but get it diagnosed.

issues.t: VTEC solenoid leaks oil or sets engine codes
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the back of the engine, a check engine light, rough running, or the engine lacking power above about 2,500 rpm.
issues.why: The VTEC solenoid and its gasket on the back of the cylinder head leak oil, and the solenoid or its pressure switch can fail. Some owners also report oil dilution after a major leak.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Replacing the gasket early is a simple fix; a failed solenoid needs a new assembly.

issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire code, rough idle, or shaking under load.
issues.why: The 2.4L engine has screw-type valve adjusters that need checking. If the valves tighten up over time, they do not seal fully and cause misfires.
issues.next: Have the valve clearances checked and adjusted. Replace plugs at the same time if they are due.

issues.sym: Strong vibration at idle or when accelerating, a clunk when shifting into gear, or a groan from the engine area.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts wear out and crack with age, so engine movement reaches the cabin.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Replace any that are cracked or collapsed.

issues.t: Key will not turn or go into the ignition
issues.sym: The key is hard to insert or turn, the car starts only sometimes, or the green key light flashes and the engine will not start.
issues.why: The ignition lock cylinder wears and the ignition switch can fail. The 2003 model has the most complaints.
issues.next: Do not force the key. Have the lock cylinder or ignition switch replaced; the key may need to be programmed at a dealer.

issues.t: Key will not go into the door locks
issues.sym: The key will not slide into the driver door lock, or it goes in but will not turn.
issues.why: The door lock cylinders wear and the tumblers stick. Honda released revised lock tumblers.
issues.next: Lubricating the lock can help. If not, have the lock cylinder replaced.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails or A/C cuts in and out
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, cools only sometimes, or the compressor makes noise.
issues.why: The A/C compressor or its clutch wears out, and a failing A/C relay can make the system cut in and out.
issues.next: Have the A/C relay and refrigerant checked first. A failed compressor needs a new compressor plus a system flush.

issues.t: Rear differential groans on turns or seizes (4WD)
issues.sym: A groan or shudder from the back when turning slowly, or grinding noise. Some neglected units leak and seize.
issues.why: The Real Time 4WD rear differential uses Honda Dual Pump fluid that wears out. Without fluid changes, its clutches chatter and bearings wear. A slow leak can run it dry.
issues.next: Change the rear differential fluid with Honda Dual Pump fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles, and check for leaks.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or harsh shifts
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, flaring rpm between gears, or the car not moving in Drive.
issues.why: Early Elements used a 4-speed automatic that owners report wearing out, and worn mounts, old fluid or shift solenoids can cause harsh shifting.
issues.next: Change the fluid with Honda ATF and have codes read. If it slips, get a transmission diagnosis before it fails.

issues.sym: The speedometer or tachometer needle drops off or points the wrong way, sometimes with a bright light from the gauges.
issues.why: Owners of 2007 Elements report the gauge needles coming loose, often after a bump.
issues.next: Have the gauge cluster repaired or replaced; a reattached needle may not read correctly.

issues.sym: Squealing or grinding brakes and pads that need replacing at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners of these years report pads and rotors wearing out much sooner than expected.
issues.next: Check pad thickness at each oil change and replace pads before they reach the metal.

issues.sym: Oil drips at the back of the engine or an oil pressure light that flickers.
issues.why: The oil pressure switch on the engine block wears and leaks oil.
issues.next: Have the switch replaced; it is a simple part. Keep the oil topped off.
